request.spec: The steward's dashboard counts are now over the sheet and all its descendants.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The steward's dashboard counts are now over the sheet and all its descendants.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The steward's dashboard counts (pending, in review, overdue) now cover the sheet plus all its descendants. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**Server** (`rollup/RollupService.java`)
- Each sheet's snapshot now also records how many of its counted claims are overdue. It uses the same overdue check the per-person figures already used.
- The descendant figures sent to the browser now include that overdue count, summed across all descendant sheets. The consolidated figures sum it across the whole tree, the sheet itself included.

**Front end** (`features/people/people.ts`)
- The dashboard adds the descendants' figures to the sheet's own counts. Pending and in-review come from the per-status claim counts the page already loads for descendants. Overdue comes from the new count.
- It's still only shown to stewards.

Nothing was stored differently, so no database migration was needed, and no audit records changed.

The descendants' pending and in-review numbers use the server's per-status counts, which include every claim on those sheets. That's the same source the existing consolidated-figures section already uses.
